definition: Horovod is a free and open-source distributed deep learning training framework for TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch and Apache MXNet.
details: It is designed to scale existing single-GPU training scripts to efficiently run on multiple GPUs and computer nodes with minimal code changes, using synchronous data-parallel training based on the ring-allreduce communication pattern. Horovod was initially developed at Uber and released as an open-source project in 2017, and is now hosted by the LF AI & Data Foundation, a project of the Linux Foundation.

explainer.lead: Horovod is a free, open-source distributed deep learning training framework for TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, and Apache MXNet. It matters because it scales existing single-GPU scripts to many GPUs and nodes with minimal code changes.

tiers.eli5: It is a tool that lets one training job spread across many computers so it finishes faster, without rewriting everything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use synchronous data-parallel training based on the ring-allreduce communication pattern to distribute work across GPUs and nodes. A pitfall is that scaling depends on efficient allreduce communication across the cluster.
tiers.paperLevel: It performs synchronous data-parallel training using ring-allreduce communication, extending single-GPU scripts to multiple GPUs and nodes. Its efficiency depends on the communication pattern across devices.

explainer.example: A team takes a PyTorch script that trains on one GPU, applies minimal changes, and runs it across many GPUs on several nodes with Horovod.
